english: Let $F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $F(x)=4x^{4}-2x^{3}-3x^{2}$, and let $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $g(x)=\max\{F(x),F(-x)\}$. Then the distance between the points of inflection of the curve $y=g(x)$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $F(x)=4x^{4}-2x^{3}-3x^{2}$ द्वारा परिभाषित है, तथा $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $g(x)=\max\{F(x),F(-x)\}$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। तब वक्र $y=g(x)$ के नति-परिवर्तन बिन्दुओं (points of inflection) के बीच की दूरी ______ है।
solution: $g''$ changes sign only at $|x|=\frac14$; at $x=0$, $g''(0)=-6<0$ on both sides, so $0$ is not a point of inflection.
Points of inflection: $x=\pm\frac14$, both with $y=g\left(\frac14\right)$; distance $=\frac12=0.5$
solution_full: For $x>0$ this is negative, so $g(x)=F(-x)$; for $x<0$ it is positive, so $g(x)=F(x)=F(-|x|)$. Hence $g(x)=F(-|x|)=4x^{4}+2|x|^{3}-3x^{2}$ for all $x$: the graph is the part of $y=F(x)$ for $x\le0$ together with its mirror image in the $y$-axis (it is $F(-|x|)$, not $F(|x|)$).

$g$ is even. For $x>0$, $g'(x)=16x^{3}+6x^{2}-6x$ and $g''(x)=48x^{2}+12x-6$; by symmetry $g''(x)=48x^{2}+12|x|-6$ for all $x$, and $g$ is twice differentiable at $0$ ($g'(0)=0$, $g''(0)=-6$ from both sides).

Thus the concavity changes exactly at $x=\pm\frac14$; at $x=0$ the curve is concave down on both sides (a local maximum), so it is not a point of inflection. (Using $F(|x|)$ by mistake would give $x=\pm\frac12$ and the wrong distance $1$.)

The inflection points are $\left(\pm\frac14,g\left(\frac14\right)\right)$ with $g\left(\frac14\right)=\frac{4}{256}+\frac{2}{64}-\frac{3}{16}=-\frac{9}{64}$; they have equal ordinates, so the distance between them is $\frac14-\left(-\frac14\right)=\frac12=0.5$.
originality_note: New: the maximum of a quartic and its mirror image is F(-|x|), so the inflection points come from the left half of F, not the right (way 2: a function defined by a max construction). Closest known: points of inflection of f(|x|) for a polynomial f. Different because: deciding which half survives the max (sign of the odd part -4x^3) is the key step, and x = 0 must be rejected as an inflection point.

concept_use.Concavity, Convexity & Points of Inflect: Sign of g''(x) = 6(4|x|-1)(2|x|+1) changes only at |x| = 1/4; no change at 0.
concept_use.Graphs of |f(x)|, f(|x|), |f(|x|)| and m: max{F(x), F(-x)} = F(-|x|) because F(x) - F(-x) = -4x^3, the reflected left half of the graph.

Exactly two inflection points, at equal height, so 'the distance between' is well defined. No change.
key_step: Identify max{F(x),F(-x)} = F(-|x|) from the odd part, then find the sign changes of g''.
justification: Two ideas linked (deciding the max via the odd part, then second-derivative sign analysis with the trap at x = 0 and the F(|x|) trap); numerical, comparable to 2026-P1-Q1 (L3), less than the parity insight of 2021-P2-Q9 (L4).
